body:
The patched methods currently don't survive when the script is reloaded. I wonder whether this might be a problem during the development in practice, because hot reloading can destroy the mod while developing it.

Similarly the modded game can trigger reloads e.g while loading a content pack, but that's a rare occurence so I guess that would be fine for a mod loader to catch.
What is the difference between the patch method and the .pck patch files?

Although I see potential in this feature, I no longer want to continue working on it because:

1. This is currently more of a proof of concept. To properly support this feature (with the potential removal of its experimental status), some considerations need to be made (whether to provide the ability to inspect and/or remove modifiers, how it should behave in edge cases, etc.).
2. I'm not sure that with the current state of the GDScript team it's possible to gather the necessary consensus to promote such features. While this is just an experimental API and not an explicit language feature, it still has some implications for the language design.

If the maintainers and the community show more interest in this feature, I can restore this PR (or someone else can do so, crediting me as a co-author). But at the moment, I see no point in maintaining this PR.

I'll say that I've been waiting with baited breath for this PR. To avoid the `class_name` issues linked in the first post, as part of mod support we've had to do a dramatic project reorganization converting all our `class_name` util scripts into dozens of autoloads so they're available for extending. This isn't possible for many of our core files, so I've been holding out hope for this PR.
It's very understandable that it'd be closed if there aren't currently a lot of resources for design & implementation, but I just wanted to voice that there is a need for some kind of eventual solution. 🙏
